another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'd be happy to help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start by asking: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - I'm not entirely sure of his exact age at the moment. I know he's a teenager, somewhere between 15 and 19, but I don't have his exact age to hand right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Knowing Alex's exact age is quite important because the rules change significantly at age 16. 

Let me ask you this: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?**

This will help me understand his situation better, even if we don't have his exact age right now.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm afraid I don't know whether he's in any education or training at the moment. I don't have that information available.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask some other important questions to assess your eligibility.

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Let me ask a few more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now let me ask:

**Are you currently the person responsible for Alex's care? By this, I mean are you the one providing for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm the one looking after Alex and responsible for all his day-to-day needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. A couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.text: No, he doesn't work 24 hours a week or anything like that, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one more important question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just living here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me review what you've told me about your situation with Alex:

**What I know:**
- Alex is your son who lives at home with you in Leeds
- He's a teenager (between 15-19 years old, but exact age unknown)
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care and needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- He's not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation

**The issue:** The critical missing information is Alex's exact age and whether he's in approved education or training. This is crucial because:

- If Alex is **under 16**, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit regardless of his education status

- If Alex is **16 or over** and **not in approved education or training**, you would not qualify (unless he's in the 20-week grace period after leaving education)

Without knowing Alex's exact age and education status, I cannot definitively determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. Would you be able to find out either his exact age or whether he's currently in education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand that you need more information, but I'm afraid I simply don't have those details available right now - neither his exact age nor whether he's in education or training. Is there any way to proceed with the claim or check eligibility without that information?

I understand your situation, and I appreciate you answering all the questions you could. Unfortunately, without knowing Alex's exact age or his education/training status, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit.

The reason this information is essential is because the eligibility rules fundamentally change at age 16:

- Children 16-19: only qualify if in approved education or training

Since Alex falls somewhere in the 15-19 age range and you don't have information about either his exact age or education status, I cannot determine with certainty whether an application would be successful.

**My recommendation:** Before proceeding with a claim, you would need to obtain either:
1. Alex's exact age/date of birth, OR
2. Confirmation of whether he's currently in approved education or training

Once you have this information, you would be in a much better position to apply for Child Benefit or I could give you a definitive answer about eligibility.

Let me now provide my assessment based on the information available:
